correctness.rationale: For the independent samples under the common atomless null, anchoring a named first-sample point yields equally likely assignments of the other first-sample label positions. These positions and the weak gap compositions are in bijection. Samplewise, the zeros are the only negative deviations when n/m<=1, so R=2nZ/m. Each occupied gap contributes one second-sample run, matched by one first-sample run, proving the stated affine equivalence, with matched tie treatment. The null has P(S1=0)=(m-1)/(m+n-1), P(S1=S2=0)=(m-1)(m-2)/((m+n-1)(m+n-2)), including m=2. The factorial generating identities give E Q=n+2n(n-1)/(m+1) and its zero-conditioned version by replacing m with m-1. For Var Q, if P_k is the ratio of falling n of order k to rising m of order k, expansion gives (24m+4m(m-1))P_4+24mP_3+4mP_2-(2mP_2)^2, which factors as in the source. The covariance follows from the mean shift multiplied by m P(S1=0); both variances and covariance are positive. Verified the denominator-minus-numerator factor and balanced successive-difference factor; the cubic is positive at 2 and has positive derivative for s>=2. Counting positive compositions gives the balanced vacancy law; leading powers give both limiting statements. Independent exact replay python3 -B /workspace/evidence/check_2.py checks separator configurations for 28 pairs with 2<=n<=m<=8. All-parameter correctness uses the moment proof, not these finite checks. This is dependence in second moments and optimal linear prediction, not a full joint law or incremental power theorem.
